v84: FAILS - hermesc rejects the `class` keyword entirely ("invalid statement
     encountered"): no IRGen lowering for classes in this lineage — same root
     cause as 32-class-basic .. 36-class-getters-setters, see
     36-class-getters-setters/versions.txt for the full analysis.
v94: FAILS - identical, same root cause.
v96: FAILS - identical, same root cause.
v98: OK - compiles (Static Hermes lineage); the decompiled output is KNOWN
     WRONG at this version, see below.
v99: OK - compiles; the decompiled output is KNOWN WRONG at this version, see
     below.

This fixture is the minimal reproducer for the bug behind adversarial fixture
21-class-private-fields (CONSOLIDATION 26 triage, docs/BUGS.md): Static
Hermes lowers a class getter/setter PAIR as two DefineOwnGetterSetterByVal
instructions, each with the other half `undefined`, and `src/emit/lower.ts`
emits both halves as a full `Object.defineProperty(o, k, {get, set})`, so the
second one clobbers the first (`get after pair: undefined`). The Hermes VM
(`caseDefineOwnGetterSetterByVal`, Interpreter-slowpaths.cpp) only sets
`setGetter`/`setSetter` for the non-undefined operand and leaves the other
half alone. Object-literal accessor pairs are unaffected at every version
(hermesc merges them into ONE instruction even when other keys sit between the
two halves — verified v94 and v99), which is why 36-class-getters-setters'
`temp` object passes and why this is a v98/v99 class-only bug.

Until fixed, v98/v99 are excluded from the gate/hardened/sweep runs via
`KNOWN_WRONG_OUTPUT` in src/harness/tiers.ts (the same expected-failure
mechanism as 01-if-else-chain.min); delete those two entries once the emit fix
lands and this fixture becomes an ordinary PASS.
